tasks.reasoning:
The STT endpoint is called directly over raw HTTP. The usage map does not show which model, if any, is sent. If none is sent, behaviour already changed on 2026-06-29. If saarika:v2.5 is sent, that model is slated for deprecation. The migration agent should read api/stt.js and set model explicitly to saaras:v3 (with mode='transcribe' if needed). It should then confirm the response fields the code reads (e.g. transcript, language_code) are unchanged. This is uncertain because the request body was not captured.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- sarvam:2026-saarika-v2-5-deprecated (model-retirement): saarika:v2.5 STT model deprecated (removal date not given); use saaras:v3/v4. The fix sets an explicit STT model on api/stt.js. Pinning saaras:v3, not saarika:v2.5, also moves the call off the deprecated Saarika v2.5 model. If the code already passes saarika:v2.5, this same edit replaces it.

## Supabase disables a subset of TLS 1.2 ciphers on project HTTP APIs (*.supabase.co); old clients may fail [Not affected]

### Change

demo/server.js and demo/server_old.js call Supabase REST with Node's global fetch. There is no custom https.Agent, cipher list, minVersion or secureProtocol setting in demo/. Node's built-in TLS (Node 22 in the sandbox) negotiates TLS 1.3 or modern TLS 1.2 ciphers, so the disabled TLS 1.2 ciphers should not affect these calls. No code was changed.

No files changed.

### Why

Supabase will disable a subset of TLS 1.2 ciphers on 2026-11-10. This repo's clients don't pin old ciphers or TLS versions, so nothing in the code forces a change.

> Supabase will be disabling a subset of TLS 1.2 ciphers on project HTTP APIs on November 10, 2026.

Source: https://supabase.com/changelog

### Proof

No checks were run.

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The production Node runtime version was not checked; a very old runtime could fail the handshake.
- I did not read the Supabase changelog entry or docs for the exact list of disabled ciphers.
- I did not search server_old.js separately for fetch usage; the grep covered all of demo/ and found no TLS settings.
- No checks were run.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.
